newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fx easing to help S.African firms compete - Manuel.
newsitem.headline: Fx easing to help S.African firms compete - Manuel.

text.p: Government moves to ease foreign exchange controls, announced in Wednesday's budget, will help South African companies compete more effectively in the global market, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday.

"If South African firms remain out of the race that is becoming increasingly global, many of our firms who should move to a higher stage of competitiveness are going to whither and die," he told parliament's finance committee.

The budget set out a series of measures to help corporates, including giving them the ability to raise foreign funding on the strength of South African balance sheets and allowing the retention of foreign currency for up to 30 days.

As far as individuals were concerned, Manuel said he did not envisage that the plan to let them invest limited amounts offshore or hold foreign currency bank accounts from July 1 would lead to a significant increase in demand for dollars.
"I've heard it said that the smart money already left and wants to come home...So we don't see a surge in demand."

Unlocking the blocked funds of emigrants, which analysts estimate at around 15 billion rand, was more problematic since the owners lived abroad and would clearly want to take the cash out, with potentially disastrous consequences for foreign reserves.
Some commentators had suggested that Manuel would announce in the budget a special bond for emigrants which would give them access to blocked funds after a number of years.
But Manuel said it was not a priority at present: "It wasn't actually on our agenda to do that now."
